questions.question: If the number x4562 is divisible by 9, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
For a number to be divisible by 9, the sum of digits should be divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum of digits = x + 4 + 5 + 6 + 2 = 17 + x

If, x = 1, sum of digits will be 18, which is a multiple of 9.

For sum of the digits to be 27 (next multiple of 9), x = 10, which is not possible.

∴ Value of x is 1.

questions.question: Out of three pipes the first two can fill an empty tank in 9 hours and 18 hours, respectively while the third can drain the filled tank in 15 hours. If all the three pipes are opened when the tank is empty, after how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
Let the amount of work required to done to fill a tank be 90 units (L.C.M of 9, 18 and 15)

⇒ Amount of work done by pipe A in 1 hour = 90/9 = 10 units

⇒ Amount of work done by pipe B in 1 hour = 90/18 = 5 units

⇒ Amount of work done by pipe C in 1 hour = 90/(-15) = -6 units

If all three work together, amount of work done in 1 hour will be = 10 + 5 – 6 = 9 units

∴ Time required for complete work = Total work/Work done in 1 hour = 90/9 = 10 hours.

questions.question:
Decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the information given the statement.

**Statement:**

People are often seen selling things on the footpath in busy market areas.

**Conclusions: **

1. Take help of police to clear the footpath from these vendors.

2. Some place should be allotted to these vendors to sell their goods without blocking the footpath.
questions.solution:
Conclusion 2 logically follows from the given statement, as it suggests a solution that accommodates the vendors while ensuring that the footpath remains clear for pedestrians.

Conclusion 1 does not necessarily follow from the given statement, as it suggests a possible action but does not consider whether it is a practical or desirable solution. Additionally, it assumes that the vendors are causing a problem that requires police intervention, which may not be the case.

Therefore, conclusion 1 does not logically follow from the given statement.

questions.question: One of the roots of the equation x² – 6x + k = 0 is x = 2. The other root is:
questions.solution:

⇒ (2)² – 6(2) + k = 0

⇒ 4 – 12 + k = 0

⇒ K = 8

The equation becomes, x² – 6x + 8 = 0

⇒ x² – 4x – 2x + 8 = 0

⇒ x(x – 4) – 2(x – 4) = 0

∴ The other root is, x = 4.

questions.question: What is the upward force exerted by water called ?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Archimedes principle:

the principle of Archimedes states “When a body is immersed in a liquid, an upward thrust, equal to the weight of the liquid displaced, acts on it.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/965af0fe078d8cd5de7d0224fb4dbf687b4efa01717a8d927db4a1b4462666bc.png] 

Thus, when a solid is fully immersed in a liquid, it loses weight which is equal to the weight of the liquid it displaces.

i.e., Apperent weight = actual weight - buoyant force = mg - rho gV

where m is mass of the object, ρ is the density of the fluid

Hence if there is no gravity, there is no Upward Thrust.

The upward force applied on the object is called buoyant force or upward thrust or buoyancy of liquid.

Here,

ρ = density of liquid

g = acceleration due to gravity

V = volume of liquid displaced by the object

__Explanation:__

__
 
• A body that is completely or partially submerged in fluid experiences an upward force called the **Buoyant Force**__.
 
• The buoyant force is equal in magnitude to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
• This principle can be used to explain why ships, loaded with millions of kilograms of cargo, are able to float.

questions.question: P, Q and R are channels which discharge solutions A, B, C respectively in a tank. When the tank is empty and all the three channels are opened what is the proportion of the solution C in the tank after 3 minutes, if the channels P, Q and R can fill the tank from empty to full in 30 minutes and 20 minutes and 10 minutes respectively when they are opened one at a time.
questions.solution:
Discharge rate is given by = Discharge volume/Time taken

Let the volume of tank be ‘X’ litres.

⇒ Discharge rate of channel P = X/30

⇒ Discharge rate of channel Q = X/20

⇒ Discharge rate of channel R = X/10

⇒ Volume of water discharged by channel P in 3 minutes = (X × 3)/30

⇒ Volume of water discharged by channel Q in 3 minutes = (X × 3)/20

⇒ Volume of water discharged by channel R in 3 minutes = (X × 3)/10

∴ Proportion of solution ‘C’ discharged by channel R = (3X/10)/(3X/30 + 3X/20 + 3X/10)

⇒ (3X/10)/(3X/30 + 3X/20 + 3X/10) = (1/10)/(1/30 + 1/20 + 1/10)

⇒ (1/10)/(1/30 + 1/20 + 1/10) = (1/10)/[(2 + 3 + 6)/60) = 60/(10 × 11) = 6/11

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The times taken by P, Q, and R are 30, 20, and 10 minutes respectively. We find the LCM to harmonize their filling rates on a common scale.

LCM of 30, 20, and 10 is 60.

Capacity of Channel P = 60/30 = 2 unit per min

 Capacity of Channel P = 60/20 = 3 unit per min

Capacity of Channel P = 60/10 = 6 unit per min

Combined rate per minute = 2 + 3 + 6 = 11 Unit per min

In 3 minutes, the total volume filled by all channels = 11 × 3 = 33 Unit

According to the Question, 

The proportion of the solution C in the tank after 3 minutes

⇒ 18/33 

⇒ 6/11

**∴ After 3 minutes, the proportion of solution C in the tank is 6/11.**

Assume an equilateral triangle with sides ‘3x’.

3 small equilateral triangles are formed at the vertices of the bigger triangle each with sides ‘x’.

⇒ Area of the bigger triangle = (3)¹/²/4 × (3x)² = 9x² × (3)¹/²/4

⇒ Area of the smaller triangles = (3)¹/²/4 × x²

⇒ Area of 3 smaller triangles combined = 3x² × (3)¹/²/4

⇒ Area of the rest of the bigger triangle = 9x² × (3)¹/²/4 – 3x² × (3)¹/²/4 = 6x² × (3)¹/²/4

∴ Required ratio = (3x² × (3)¹/²/4) ∶ (6x² × (3)¹/²/4) = 1 : 2

questions.question: Identify the use of the isotope of uranium.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Fuel in nuclear reactors**

**__Explanation:-__**

**Treatment of cancer:**

 
• For the treatment of cancer, medical professionals commonly use isotopes like Cobalt-60, Iodine-131, and Radium-223. These isotopes emit radiation that can target and destroy cancerous cells.
 
• Cobalt-60: Used in radiation therapy to treat various types of cancer.

**Fuel in airplanes:**

 
• Airplanes typically use aviation fuel, which is a type of specialized kerosene, rather than nuclear fuels.
 
• Uranium isotopes are not used as fuel in conventional airplanes.

**Treatment of goiter:**

 
• Goiter, an enlargement of the thyroid gland, is commonly treated with iodine isotopes, specifically Iodine-131. It can be used to treat overactive thyroid tissue, shrinking the gland and reducing the size of the goiter.

**Fuel in nuclear reactors:**

 
• Uranium-235 and Uranium-238 are used in nuclear reactors. Uranium-235, in particular, is a fissile isotope that can sustain a nuclear chain reaction, releasing a significant amount of energy used to generate electricity in nuclear power plants.
 
• This is the primary and well-known use of uranium isotopes.

 
• **U-235 **is an isotope of uranium which can sustain a fission chain reaction, releasing large amounts of energy
 
• Therefore it is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors

questions.question:
Consider the following question and decide whether any of the statements among the given statements are adequate to answer that question.

What is the total number of students in the class?

**Statements:**

1. Mr X’s rank was 15th from the top in the class.

2. Mr X’s rank was 26th from the bottom of the class.

options.text: Both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.
2 alone is sufficient while 1 alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
1 alone is sufficient while 2 alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Either 1 or 2 is sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
Statement 1: Mr. X’s rank was 15th from the top in the class. Not sufficient to answer the question.

Statement 2: Mr. X’s rank was 26th from the bottom in the class. Not sufficient to answer the question.

By combining statement 1 and statement 2 we conclude that,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5da433d8d2ac3e0b10931d153e8025e18a1839fd824c89859f45354b7a55a9e8.png] 

Total number of students = 15 + 26 - 1 = 40

Hence, both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.

questions.question: The price of a Television is Rs. 14000 inclusive of VAT. If the rate of VAT is 12%, find the basic price of the television.
questions.solution:
Let the basic price of television be ‘x’.

The price after 12% VAT becomes ‘1.12x’

⇒ 1.12 × x = 14000

⇒ x = 14000/1.12

∴ Basic price, x = Rs. 12,500

questions.question:
Consider the argument and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit.

**Argument:**

A father advised his son that the shortest route between Chennai and Mangalore is via Bengaluru.

**Assumptions:**

1. Son wishes to go to Mangalore.

2. Father gives advice to everyone.
questions.solution:
Father is advising his son about the shortest route to Mangalore. It implies that the son is planning or wishes to go to Mangalore. So, assumption 1 is implicit. Here, the father is giving advice to his son. Nothing is mentioned about whether he gives advice to anyone else. So, assumption 2 is not implicit.

Hence, only assumption 1 is implicit.

Watt is a small unit that's why kilowatt-hour is used as the unit for electrical energy.

• One watt is defined as the energy consumption rate of one joule per second.

• It is completely different from "Units" which measures the electricity provided to our houses.1 Unit is 1000 watt-hour.

questions.question: A man misses a train by 1 hour if he travels at a speed of 4 kmph, if he had increased his speed to 5 kmph, he would have still missed the train by 24 minutes. At what speed should he have travelled so that he reached the station exactly on time?
questions.solution:
In both the cases, distance ‘d’ travelled is same. When he travels at 5 kmph, he reached the station 36 min earlier than when he travels at 4 kmph.

Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ d/5 + 36/60 = d/4

⇒ d/4 – d/5 = 36/60

⇒ d/20 = 36/60

⇒ d = 12 km.

When he travels at 4 kmph, he reaches after 3 hours and still is late by 1 hour. Therefore, he has to reach station in 2 hours.

∴ Required speed = 12/2 = 6 kmph
